note: htmlParseNameComplex() (HTMLparser.c) returns `xmlDictLookup(ctxt->dict, ctxt->input->cur - len, len)` with no check that `ctxt->input->cur - len` is still within the input buffer -- for a crafted HTML document the accumulated len can exceed the distance from ctxt->input->base to ctxt->input->cur, so the pointer/length pair handed to the dictionary already points before the start of the allocation. xmlDictLookup forwards it unchanged into xmlDictAddString (dict.c), whose `memcpy(pool->free, name, namelen)` then reads namelen bytes starting at that out-of-bounds pointer.

traces.message: return(xmlDictLookup(ctxt->dict, ctxt->input->cur - len, len)); -- cur - len computed with no check against ctxt->input->base, can point before the start of the input buffer
memcpy(pool->free, name, namelen); in xmlDictAddString -- reads namelen bytes from the unguarded pointer produced above.
